nt: The author is speaking as if the **adversary** had actually **stood up**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the adversary took action]

The Hebrew word “satan” means “adversary.” The Old Testament uses the word in that specific sense in several places, for example, [1 Kings 11:14](../../1ki/11/14.md), “Yahweh raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite.” In the book of Job, there is a character called “the satan” or “the adversary.” This seems to be a created angelic being who opposes righteous people and accuses them before God of having wrong motives. Many interpreters of the book of Job identify this character with Satan, the devil, and many interpreters believe that the author is describing that same figure here. The UST uses a general expression. You can decide how to translate this term in your own translation.
